body.estimand_functional: \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{eff}}=\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{CM}}-\widehat b_{\mathrm{cyc}}^{\prime}\widehat K^{-1}\widehat\kappa\), \(\widehat V=\widehat h^{\star\prime}\widehat\Omega\widehat h^{\star}\), \(\phi^{\star}=h^{\star\prime}Z\), and \(\Gamma=b_{\mathrm{cyc}}^{\prime}K^{-1}b_{\mathrm{cyc}}\), with the cycle correction empty when \(q=0\)

sampling_model.design: Fixed \(T\), deterministic cohort strata, and known target weights \(p_g\).
sampling_model.units: Within each \(g\in C\), \(n_g\) units are independent and identically distributed; cohort samples are mutually independent and \(n_g/N\to p_g>0\).
sampling_model.treatment: The required cohort \(\infty\in C\) is never treated; each \(g<\infty\) first receives treatment at \(t=g\), and no anticipation and consistency connect observed and potential outcomes.
sampling_model.overlap: The full-panel untreated graph \(H_U\) contains the canonical spanning tree through cohort \(\infty\), is connected, and has \(D\ne\varnothing\); all cohort shares are positive.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Compute \(\overline Y_g\), \(\widehat p_g\), and \(\widehat\Sigma_g\) from each cohort; fit the normalized fixed-dimensional untreated cohort-mean PPML model, then form \(\widehat R,\widehat b_{\mathrm{cyc}},\widehat K,\widehat h^{\star}\), and \(\widehat V\) on \(\mathcal E_N\). No cross-fitting is required.

Theorem 34 identifies rank-one circuit graphs as simple even cycles and Remark 35 turns their positive-entry relations into alternating log-linear equations.
Proposition 2.1 gives covariance-dependent variance-minimizing coefficients within a design-based class of additive staggered-rollout estimators.
Theorems 3.1--3.2 derive efficient influence functions for additive DiD and event-study parameters under sequential parallel-trends moment restrictions.
Theorems 1--2 characterize efficient linear unbiased additive event-study estimation and its imputation representation under the paper's error model.

Sections 2--3 specify individual-level fully interacted nonlinear conditional means, impute individual untreated counterfactuals, and show canonical-link equality of imputation and pooled quasi-likelihood estimates of cohort--time average treatment effects.

body.tldr: In a fixed-horizon proportional staggered panel with the required never-treated cohort \(\infty\in C\), the untreated rank-one mean restrictions have one independent weighted tangent direction per graph cycle. A bounded truncation-and-correction construction proves tangent equality for the explicitly mean-differentiable finite-fourth-moment experiment, and the canonical gradient subtracts the covariance projection of a distinct cohort-mean PPML-imputation influence function onto those directions. This cohort-mean estimator is efficient for every bounded legal covariance law exactly when the untreated graph is acyclic; with cycle rank \(q>0\), the exceptional efficient laws satisfy exactly \(q\) primitive alternating covariance balances, while an explicit support-preserving family and a positive-radius ambient covariance ball certify strictly positive exact quadratic loss. A feasible cycle correction attains the bound and supports pointwise Wald inference. Moreau--Kastler's individual fixed-effects imputation and Wooldridge's fully interacted individual-level nonlinear imputation inform the construction but are not identified with it outside an explicit aggregation boundary.

project_justification.gap: Moreau--Kastler (2025) fits untreated individual fixed effects and aggregates individual counterfactual predictions into PTT, while Wooldridge (2023) develops fully interacted individual-level nonlinear imputation for cohort--time average treatment effects. Neither provides an efficiency frontier for the distinct cohort-mean rank-one PPML score; existing efficient staggered-DiD results are additive, and rank-one completion results do not classify causal-estimator efficiency.
project_justification.niche: The positive cohort-mean rank-one untreated manifold makes graph cycles simultaneously the overidentifying restrictions and the covariance-sensitive precision directions, permitting an exact topology-level efficiency frontier without claiming equivalence to richer individual-level counterfactual specifications.
project_justification.fill: The project proves weighted-cycle tangent completeness by a support-preserving score construction, derives and attains the canonical gradient with explicit sample covariance functionals, differentiates the cohort-mean PPML-imputation estimator, characterizes its efficient covariance laws by \(q\) primitive balances, and certifies strict loss on a realizable bounded family and a positive-radius ambient covariance neighborhood. A boundary proposition supplies the exact profiling conditions under which the Moreau--Kastler individual estimator collapses to the cohort-mean estimator.

body.related_work: Moreau--Kastler (2025, Section 3.2.2, equations 3.13--3.14) estimates individual fixed effects and time effects by PPML on never-treated and not-yet-treated individual observations, predicts individual untreated counterfactuals, and aggregates the treated observed-to-predicted ratio; the estimator analyzed here instead fits a cohort-mean rank-one score and is therefore only informed by that paper. The aggregation-bridge proposition isolates exact equality under equal observation weights, no covariates or offsets, balanced individual panels, and target shares equal to sample shares. Wooldridge (2023, Sections 2--3, especially equations 3.12--3.13 and the canonical-link discussion) specifies fully interacted individual-level nonlinear conditional means, obtains individual counterfactual predictions and cohort--time effects, and proves imputation--pooled quasi-likelihood equivalence; it neither uses the cohort-mean rank-one score nor targets the same aggregate ratio. Ciani and Fisher (2019, printed page 7, Section 3.1) state that PPML may fail to be the most efficient estimator, and Appendix B reports simulations showing the efficiency loss; Appendix C is instead the empirical Educational Maintenance Allowance application. The present theorem strictly sharpens that qualitative possibility for the stated cohort-mean estimator to an acyclic if-and-only-if frontier and exact codimension. Király, Theran, and Tomioka (2015, Theorem 34 and Remark 35) show that rank-one matrix circuits are even cycles; their algebraic relation informs the complete weighted tangent restriction basis. Chamberlain (1987) and Newey (1990) supply projection and tangent-score tools, but not the nonnegative support-preserving submodel construction. Roth and Sant'Anna (2023, Proposition 2.1), Borusyak, Jaravel, and Spiess (2024, Theorems 1--2), and Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie (2025, Theorems 3.1--3.2) develop covariance-aware efficiency for additive staggered DiD rather than the nonlinear PTT ratio and its graph-topological frontier. Wooldridge (1999) supplies distribution-free fixed-effects Poisson theory. Nagengast and Yotov (2025) and Menkhoff and Miethe (2019) are concrete bilateral-data consumers, although their richer dependence and fixed effects remain outside the benchmark theorem.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Because \(\infty\in C\) and the panel is fully observed, \(q=\sum_{g<\infty}(g-2)\); the topology theorem does not claim arbitrary missing-panel graph generality. There is no positive loss bound uniform over all inefficient laws because \(\Gamma(x)\to0\) as \(x\to0\). Singular covariance blocks, zero mean cells, random cohort shares, growing \(T\), unbalanced panels, and dyadic shared-country dependence are outside the formal model. The finite-fourth-moment tangent result is pointwise for the explicitly mean-differentiable differentiable-in-quadratic-mean experiment and uses bounded support-preserving submodels constructed by truncation and exact mean correction; it does not classify tail-escaping paths for which score-moment differentiation fails.
body.honest_scope: The theorem contributions concern the explicitly defined cohort-mean PPML-imputation estimator: PTT-specific weighted-cycle completeness, constructive tangent equality for the mean-differentiable finite-fourth-moment experiment, the exact rank-\(q\) primitive covariance map, the acyclic universal-efficiency equivalence, and a legal bounded family with exact quadratic loss and an ambient positive-radius strict-loss neighborhood. No general identity with Moreau--Kastler's individual fixed-effects imputation or Wooldridge's fully interacted individual-level nonlinear estimator is asserted; exact equality with the former is confined to the stated aggregation boundary. Canonical projection algebra and routine sandwich consistency are supporting machinery. The open-ended question concerns growing horizon and growing cycle rank. The admissible tree reduction uses \(C=\{2,\infty\}\) at fixed \(T\ge3\) and yields the explicit multi-post multiplicative ratio, while the exact three-period witness audits the smallest cyclic case.
